label: L-03
title: A near-zero exchangeRate turns a soft throttle into a hard brick: the stable leg rounds to zero and PhUSDNotReceived kills the whole annihilation
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.

classification.assetImpact: Liveness only, no value loss. exchangeRate = 0 as a soft 'stop paying the stable half' hard-bricks annihilation for that stablecoin; near-zero rates brick it only for small amounts, giving an amount-dependent revert whose error name points at the wrong contract.
attackPath: 2. floor(amount * rate / 1e18) truncates to zero, so the stable leg mints nothing.
3. :233's zero-guard reverts the WHOLE annihilation rather than delivering the still-valid antimatter leg.
4. The revert surfaces as PhUSDNotReceived, which reads as 'the minter failed to deliver', not 'your rate setting rounds to zero'.
classification.assumptions: Owner uses a near-zero rate as a soft throttle - a natural reading, and the same misapprehension M-04 documents.
classification.externalRequirements: An owner rate setting near zero.

justification: Low. Liveness only and owner-triggered, but the misdiagnosis cost is the surprising part: the guard is the right instinct (it catches a non-delivering minter) yet doubles as an undiagnosable configuration error pointing at an innocent contract. Footgun, honest severity Low. Adjacent to M-04 but a distinct failure mode (hard brick vs silent non-throttle).
recommendation: Either document PhUSDNotReceived as also covering 'exchangeRate rounds this amount's stable leg to zero', or bound the rate away from zero at registration/update time.

symbolic.note: recorded in symbolic-results.md as reachable only symbolically - 'a fuzzer over sensible rates would not reach it'

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues document exists for this project (knownIssuesFile/Source null, knownIssues empty, verified at HEAD) so KI suppression has no authority; no C4 known-invalid class genuinely applies; not a malicious-owner vector; ledger empty so no prior entry to reconcile against.

additionalContext.rootCause: When floor(amount * rate / 1e18) truncates to zero the stable leg mints nothing, and :233's zero-guard reverts the entire annihilation rather than delivering the still-valid antimatter leg. The guard is the right instinct (it catches a non-delivering minter) - the problem is that it doubles as an undiagnosable configuration error.
additionalContext.impact: Liveness only, no value loss. Setting rate = 0 as a soft 'stop paying the stable half' hard-bricks annihilation for that stablecoin. Near-zero rates brick it only for small amounts, producing an amount-dependent revert whose error name (PhUSDNotReceived) points at the minter failing to deliver rather than at a rate setting.
additionalContext.mightBeIntentional: Plausibly rate=0 as a per-stable kill switch - but setStablecoinEnabled(false) already exists for that and gives a clear error, so the overlap looks accidental.
